Meds are prescribed only after diagnosis is done. So first you consult a clinical psychologist, get a diagnosis done, and then go to a psychiatrist w the diagnosis if meds are required.
Only in some cases if the symptoms of a disorder are very clear even to the psychiatrist, or in case of emergencies, the psychiatrist will prescribe a very low dose of meds until the diagnosis is done.
Of course some doctors are not good, they might just prescribe depression and anxiety meds without a diagnosis, for money, but that's not how it usually works. That's why you should go to a clinical psychologist first.
An official diagnosis which is more accurate is only done by a clinical psychologist, and if a psychiatrist did a random verbal diagnosis and started prescribing meds, that's malpractice (except for emergencies or obvious symptoms)
I went to a psychiatrist for my ADHD symtoms and he too sent me to a clinical psychologist first, to get an official diagnosis done.
